record.paper_title: Achievement sets – current results and open problems
record.context_brief: Vertical sections of planar achievement sets
record.original_question: If E ⊂ ℝ² is an achievable set, must every vertical section E_x be a set of P-sums?

evidence.quote: Let E ⊂ R^2 be an achievable set. Is every vertical section Ex a set of P-sums?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(a_n)_{n=1}^\infty$ be an absolutely convergent series of vectors in $\mathbb{R}^2$, and define its achievement set (set of subsums) by
$$A((a_n)) = \Big\{ \sum_{n \in I} a_n : I \subseteq \mathbb{N} \Big\} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2.$$
Call a set $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ an achievement set (or achievable set) if $E = A((a_n))$ for some such sequence $(a_n)$ in $\mathbb{R}^2$.

Analogously, for an absolutely convergent real series $(p_n)_{n=1}^\infty$, the set of P-sums is its achievement set
$$\Big\{ \sum_{n \in I} p_n : I \subseteq \mathbb{N} \Big\} \subseteq \mathbb{R},$$
and a subset of $\mathbb{R}$ is called a set of P-sums if it arises in this way from some absolutely convergent real series.

For $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ and $x \in \mathbb{R}$, the vertical section at $x$ is
$$E_x = \{ y \in \mathbb{R} : (x,y) \in E \}.$$

Question: If $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ is an achievement set, must every nonempty vertical section $E_x$ be a set of P-sums?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is listed as an open problem in a recent survey on achievement sets (2025/2026). Web searches did not turn up any resolution in the literature; standard references on achievement sets discuss the planar/multidimensional theory but do not address this specific vertical-section question.

status_evidence.snippet: General theory of achievement sets of absolutely convergent series; no resolution of the planar vertical-section question.
